findings.title: Anchor allow-list regex matches any tag starting with 'a'
findings.body: ANCHOR_PATTERN is '</?a[^>]*>', which matches tags such as <article>, <abbr>, and <area>, not just <a>. In santizeAnchors(), matching tags are removed from the value before OWASP sanitization. If the English source and translation both contain such a non-anchor tag, it will be stripped from the checked value and can pass verification even though the tag is not allowed by the HTML policy. Use a word boundary, for example '</?a\b[^>]*>'.

findings.title: Choice formats are removed wholesale before HTML validation
findings.body: normalizeValue() replaces the whole '{n,choice,...}' expression with '...' for linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit* and error-invalid-multivalued-size. Any HTML placed inside the choice alternatives is therefore never passed to the sanitizer. For example, a malicious or malformed choice such as '{0,choice,0#<script>}' would be stripped out before validation and could pass. The choice content should be validated or sanitized rather than ignored.

findings.title: Diff substring computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.body: When reporting a sanitizer mismatch, start and end are computed independently from the beginning and end of the strings. There is no check that start + end is less than or equal to each string length. If the sanitized value is shorter and shares both prefix and suffix characters with the original value, substring(start, length - end) can have an end index before start and throw, causing the verifier to fail with an unexpected exception instead of reporting the HTML problem.

findings.title: Missing English reference file fails with RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() wraps failure to read the derived English properties file in a RuntimeException. In a Maven plugin context this produces a less controlled build failure than the MojoExecutionException used by verify(). If an expected English file is missing or the derived path is wrong, the build fails with an unchecked exception instead of a clear plugin error message.

findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax used in JavaScript account-ui bundle
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from '{{0}}', '{{1}}', '{{2}}' to '{0}' and '{2,choice,...}'. This file is a JavaScript account-ui message bundle where other parameterized messages use double-curly interpolation. Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax will not be processed by the UI i18n layer, so users are likely to see raw braces/choice text instead of a localized, formatted message.

findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax used in JavaScript admin-ui bundle
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from '{{0}}', '{{1}}', '{{2}}' to '{0}' and '{2,choice,...}'. Admin UI message bundles use double-curly interpolation elsewhere, so Java MessageFormat choice syntax is unlikely to be evaluated by the admin UI. This can break parameter substitution and pluralization for this validation message in the admin console.

findings.title: Lithuanian account message contains Italian text
findings.body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account bundle is 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the account/OTP setup page. It should be replaced with the proper Lithuanian translation.

findings.title: Lithuanian login message contains Italian text
findings.body: loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian login bundle is 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see Italian text during login TOTP setup. It should be replaced with the proper Lithuanian translation.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese bundle uses Traditional Chinese wording
findings.body: totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN.properties uses Traditional Chinese characters such as '手機上安裝以下應用程式之一'. A Simplified Chinese bundle should use Simplified characters, for example '在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：'.

findings.title: No positive tests for allowed HTML or matching anchor tags
findings.body:
The added tests only verify that illegal HTML, disallowed HTML, or changed anchors are detected. There are no tests showing that valid allowed tags such as ,
, or identical anchor tags from the English source pass without producing verifier messages. Without positive fixtures, future changes to sanitizer normalization could introduce false positives unnoticed.
